# TreeForge

**Turn filesystem directories and AI-generated folder structures into beautiful, customizable diagrams using Mermaid and Graphviz. Smart grouping, depth control, file icons, and multiple export formats.**

TreeForge reads real directories or text trees, groups similar files, and renders classic connected vertical trees or horizontal diagrams with optional boxes.

> Current release: [v0.1.0](https://github.com/SergioGilBorras/treeforge/releases/tag/v0.1.0). Download packaged distributions from GitHub Releases or install directly from the version tag.

## Gallery — generated by TreeForge

The following four SVGs with default icons are generated **from the exact same input text** using `python devtools/generate_previews.py`. The images are committed to this repository so you can inspect them on GitHub without installing anything.

| Orientation | Without boxes | With boxes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Vertical** | ![Classic vertical tree with connected branches](docs/examples/vertical-plain.svg) | ![Vertical tree with boxes](docs/examples/vertical-boxes.svg) |
| **Horizontal** | ![Horizontal tree without boxes](docs/examples/horizontal-plain.svg) | ![Horizontal tree with boxes](docs/examples/horizontal-boxes.svg) |

Native SVG draws continuous geometric branches. TXT uses the familiar `├──` and `└──` characters. The vertical layout without boxes is the default.

## Features

- Sources: filesystem, pasted AI-generated tree text, or path lists.
- Depth/node budgets; conservative numeric-prefix and file-category grouping.
- Native vertical/horizontal SVG, optional boxes, left/center horizontal alignment.
- Classic file-type icons for folders, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, JSON, ZIP, TXT, music, video and more. Optionally override icons using `--icons-dir ./icons`; configure colors by extension/category.
- Mermaid (`.mmd`) and Graphviz (`.dot`; SVG/PNG/PDF with installed `dot`).
- Python 3.10+; dependency-free Python runtime for native/Mermaid/DOT export.

## Installation

Install directly from GitHub:

```bash
python -m pip install git+https://github.com/SergioGilBorras/treeforge.git@v0.1.0
```

Alternatively, install from a source checkout with `python -m pip install .`. To build distribution artifacts locally, install `build` and run `python -m build`; the resulting files are written to `dist/`.

## CLI examples

```bash
treeforge render . --layout vertical --max-depth 3 --output vertical.svg
treeforge render . --layout vertical --boxes --icons-dir ./icons --output vertical-boxes.svg
treeforge render . --layout horizontal --align center --output horizontal.svg
treeforge render . --layout horizontal --boxes --output horizontal-boxes.svg
treeforge render . --layout horizontal --output structure.mmd
treeforge render tree.txt --input-format tree --layout vertical --output ai-tree.svg
```

## Python example

```python
from treeforge import TreeForge, TreeConfig

tree = TreeForge.from_directory(".", TreeConfig(
    max_depth=3, boxes=True,
    colors={"folder": "#376aab", "images": "#a855a0", "py": "#438b56"},
    icons_dir="./icons",
))
tree.render("structure.svg", engine="native", layout="vertical")
tree.render("structure.mmd", layout="horizontal")
```

## Developer validation and reproducible preview images

```bash
python devtools/run_validation.py
python devtools/generate_previews.py
pytest
```

`devtools/run_validation.py` creates temporary filesystem fixtures, equivalent text/path inputs, integration checks, JSON reports and an HTML gallery under ignored `validation-output/`. The preview generator writes eight SVG examples into `docs/examples/`. Neither script is bundled into the published wheel.

GitHub Actions runs the test suite on Linux, Windows and macOS with Python 3.10 and 3.12, and checks wheel and source distribution builds.
